literal: Like hair fallen from the head are people, when they have fallen from their status.
translation: People who fall from their high status of honor are like hair that has fallen from the head.
modern: தம்முடைய உயர்ந்த நிலையிலிருந்து தாழ்ந்துபோகும்போது, மனிதர்கள் தலையிலிருந்து உதிர்ந்த மயிரைப் போன்றவர் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to illustrate the loss of honor. Hair on the head is highly valued and cared for, but once it falls off, it is treated as worthless and discarded with disgust. Similarly, people who fall from their high moral standing or honorable position lose all their respect and are looked down upon by society. The comparison emphasizes that honor, once lost, reduces a person's worth to nothing.
